name: Eglon king of Moab
charge: Possessing the city of palm trees and holding Israel in servitude eighteen years
summary: Israel did evil again, and the Lord made Eglon king of Moab strong against them; Eglon allied with Ammon and Amalek, took the city of palm trees, and held Israel in service eighteen years. The same nations whose hearts melted at the report of Israel in Joshua’s day were now being strengthened against Israel for breaking the commandments. When the people cried, the Lord raised up Ehud the son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, with a double-edged dagger under his clothes and a message from God. Moab was subdued that day, and the land had rest eighty years.
offenseFull: Israel did evil again in the Lord’s sight, and the Lord made Eglon king of Moab strong against Israel because of the evil they had done (Judges 3:12-14). Read that carefully: the record says the Lord strengthened him. In Joshua’s day the hearts of those same nations melted at the report of what the Lord had done for Israel, and Rahab told the spies that terror of Israel had fallen on them and no man had any courage left (Joshua 2:9-11). Now the same Lord was strengthening a heathen king against His own people for breaking His commandments. Eglon joined with Ammon and Amalek, attacked Israel, took the city of palm trees, and Israel served him eighteen years. The king’s dominion was real, but it was never power held outside the hand of the Most High; Israel’s own disobedience had set them under him.

This is one servitude out of many. We had captivity after captivity, and there is not one nation that has nothing to answer for. While our people want to hold hands and sing along with everybody, every one of these nations played its part in our demise, and plays it to this day. Moab was not an accident of politics; Moab was a rod the Most High picked up because Israel had given Him cause.
judgmentFull: When Israel cried to the Lord, He raised up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite (Judges 3:15-26). Notice how the Lord raised up judges out of different tribes: Othniel of Judah before him, now Ehud of Benjamin. Ehud made a double-edged dagger a cubit long, strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh, and carried the tribute to Eglon, who was a very fat man. Saying he had a secret errand for the king, he got him alone in his cool upper room, told him he had a message from God for him, and drove the dagger into his belly with his left hand, and the fat closed over the blade so that he could not pull it out. He shut and locked the doors of the room and went out.

The servants found the doors locked and supposed the king was relieving himself in the inner room; they waited until they were embarrassed, then took a key and found him dead on the floor. Ehud escaped to Seirath, blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and led Israel down, telling them to follow him because the Lord had given their enemies the Moabites into their hand. They seized the fords of the Jordan toward Moab and killed about ten thousand men, all strong and able fighters, and not one escaped; so Moab was subdued that day under Israel’s hand, and the land had rest eighty years (Judges 3:27-30). The same Lord who strengthened Eglon took his dominion away the moment His people cried. After Ehud came Shamgar the son of Anath, who killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad, a farm tool ten feet long with a sharp point, and he also delivered Israel (Judges 3:31).

taught.title: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

text.text: And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord.
And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees.
So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.
And she said unto the men, I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.

For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.

And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.

But when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded: and by him the children of Israel sent a present unto Eglon the king of Moab.
But Ehud made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh.
And he brought the present unto Eglon king of Moab: and Eglon was a very fat man.
And when he had made an end to offer the present, he sent away the people that bare the present.
But he himself turned again from the quarries that were by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king: who said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him went out from him.
And Ehud came unto him; and he was sitting in a summer parlour, which he had for himself alone. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat.
And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the dagger from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly:
And the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly; and the dirt came out.
Then Ehud went forth through the porch, and shut the doors of the parlour upon him, and locked them.
When he was gone out, his servants came; and when they saw that, behold, the doors of the parlour were locked, they said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber.
And they tarried till they were ashamed: and, behold, he opened not the doors of the parlour; therefore they took a key, and opened them: and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.
And Ehud escaped while they tarried, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped unto Seirath.
And it came to pass, when he was come, that he blew a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the mount, and he before them.

And he said unto them, Follow after me: for the Lord hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. And they went down after him, and took the fords of Jordan toward Moab, and suffered not a man to pass over.
And they slew of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and there escaped not a man.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.
And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel.
